q: Explain scaled dot-product attention and why we divide by sqrt(d_k).
answer: QK^T / sqrt(d_k) keeps variance stable so softmax is not peaky; multi-head splits subspaces.

q: Encoder-only vs decoder-only vs encoder-decoder: when would you pick each?
answer: BERT-style NLU; GPT-style generation; T5/BART for seq2seq. Cost, bidirectionality, infilling.

q: Walk through DDPM forward and reverse processes. What is the noise schedule doing?
answer: Forward adds Gaussian noise to x0; reverse learns ε_θ. Schedule β_t controls SNR; too fast destroys signal.

q: How does CLIP align image and text? Contrastive loss pitfalls in production?
answer: InfoNCE on batch pairs; temperature τ. Pitfalls: batch size, false negatives, domain shift, prompt sensitivity.

q: YOLO vs two-stage detectors: latency, small objects, and NMS.
answer: One-shot grid/anchor vs RPN+refine. Small objects need FPN/higher res; NMS vs NMS-free heads.

q: What is RLHF end-to-end? Compare PPO-RLHF vs DPO.
answer: SFT → RM → PPO against KL to SFT. DPO skips RM/PPO using pairwise preference closed form.

q: LoRA vs full fine-tune vs adapters: memory, rank, and when it fails.
answer: Freeze W, train BA with rank r. Fails if task needs new capacity or tokenizer/domain shift is huge.

q: Why do ViTs need more data than ConvNets? What is patch embedding?
answer: Weak locality bias; patches flatten to tokens + pos enc. Regularization, distillation, or conv stem help.

q: GAN training instability: mode collapse and what you monitor.
answer: D too strong → vanishing grad; collapse to few modes. Watch FID, recall, loss oscillation; TTUR, R1.

q: What is KV cache? How do you trade memory vs throughput at long context?
answer: Cache K/V per layer/token. PagedAttention, GQA/MQA, quantization, sliding window, spec decode.

q: Interactive segmentation (SAM-style) vs semantic segmentation heads.
answer: Promptable mask decoder vs per-pixel classes. Data: masks vs labels; latency of image encoder.

q: BPE vs WordPiece vs Unigram: multilingual and code tokenization issues.
answer: Merge rules vs likelihood. Code/CJK: vocab waste, leading spaces, digit splits; byte fallback.
